items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: gigged with pianist Paul Cephas at the South Side Club.

ctx.x: moved on to Minneapolis and played with various leaders (Frank Hines, Eddie Barefield, etc.) at the Nest Club, also gigged with pianist Paul Cephas at the South Side Club. Lester occasionally doubled alto and baritone during the early 1930's. (In 1968, Benny Carter told this writer that he had first heard Lester Young in Minneapolis [c. 1931], and Lester was then playing alto sax.) In 1932, whilst working at the Nest Club with Frank Hines, he was signed as a member of the Original Blue Devils, after playing a…
That's wrong. He didn't quit the band. The band broke up over in Virginia. They got stranded. Some of the guys even had to hobo back to Kansas City.
